implementation_notes: Kotlin uses the Java persistence model unchanged: mutableSetOf properties with @ManyToMany plus @JoinTable on the owning entity, mappedBy on the inverse side, and the kotlin-jpa plugin generating the no-arg constructor and open members some providers still need. The provider writes link rows as the set changes, so the association table stays out of the model exactly as in Java. Choose it when the project already runs Spring Data/JPA; choose Exposed when the stack should stay Kotlin-native.
pitfalls: Without the kotlin-jpa no-arg plugin Hibernate fails on entities that have only primary constructors.
data class entities generate equals/hashCode over all properties, which recurses through both sides of the many-to-many.
The default join table name is derived from the property and entity names: rename a property and the schema changes silently unless @JoinTable is explicit.

variants.name: JetBrains Exposed reference table with the via operator
variants.implementation_notes: Exposed models the association as a table object: an intermediate Table with two reference() columns and an explicit PrimaryKey over the pair, and the entity side exposes the relationship with `by Role via UserRoleTable`. This is the pattern made visible rather than hidden - the join table is a Kotlin object the developer declares, and Exposed composes the inserts, deletes and eager loads (with()/load()) over it. Prefer it when the project wants Kotlin-only APIs and full control of the schema, and accept that the link table is part of the code.
pitfalls: The intermediate table must declare the composite primary key itself; without it Exposed inserts the same pair as often as it is assigned.
DAO references are lazy by default - iterating inside a closed transaction throws, so use with() to eager load before the transaction ends.
A via property assigned a new collection rewrites the link rows wholesale; assigning a partially loaded collection silently drops the rest.
